page0.text:
We walk up the hill.
There are more students commuting than usual, possibly because morning practices are cancelled.

page1.text:
"We still have a lot of time. It's been a while since I could take my time in the morning like this."
Sakura is beside me, walking happily.
She's been in a good mood all morning, though I'm not sure why.

page2.text:
"That's normal for me...though I don't get to go to school with you that often."
"Because the kyudo club never takes any time off."

page3.text:
"True, but morning practice is supposed to be optional, right? Most people only go once every two days or so. You should take it easy, too."
"Huh? W-wait, so if I skipped practice, you would come to school with me?"

page4.text:
"? Of course I would. We're going to the same school, so we'd be together whether you wanted to or not."
"Oh. Then...
No, I can't. I'm not good at archery, so my skills could dull if I skip even one day of practice."
Sakura sticks out her tongue in self-reprimand.

page5.text: "? I dunno about that. I don't like to compare people to each other, but your skills are outstanding for a first-year. You can afford to take a day or two off."

page6.text:
"No, I still have a lot to learn. I'll get distracted if I lose focus. I'm always losing sight of my goal.
I'm a lazy person at heart, so I have to be tough on myself every day or risk letting myself go."
Hmm...
Well, if she says so.

page7.text:
I part ways with Sakura.
The second-year classrooms are on the third floor, while Sakura and the other first-years are on the fourth floor.

page8.text:
"See you later, Senpai."
"Yeah. Don't fall asleep in class. Food coma is a thing, you know."

page9.text:
"Ahaha. You don't need to worry about that. I've already digested a fifth of this morning's breakfast!"
Sakura goes up the stairs.
I wave goodbye, and head to my own classroom.

page10.text:
It's lunch break.
Shinji is absent, and so is Issei.
...I think Issei's been recovering in the hospital ever since the Ryudou Temple incident.
In fact, there are several other students out sick, too.

page11.text:
...
...But there shouldn't be any further absences.
Caster is gone. There isn't a Servant draining life force from the people of Fuyuki anymore.
That should put an end to the mysterious comas that had the city in an uproar.

page12.text: "...Right. Everyone who Caster hurt will get better soon."

page13.text:
Time to get my head on straight.
There are four Masters left.
Tohsaka and Illya aside, I don't know what the other two Masters are like, so it's too early to relax.

page14.text:
"Ah!"
Our yelps of surprise harmonize.
Just as I step into the hallway, I suddenly run into Tohsaka.

page15.text: "Hey, what's that supposed to mean? A little rude to act like that as soon as you see me, don't you think? Or what, do you have some reason to feel guilty around me?"

page16.text:
"Right back at you. You looked just as surprised, you know.
...What was the phone call for yesterday? After you complained about me going to the temple, you demanded that I come meet you at school. You're pretty fickle, Tohsaka."

page17.text:
"Mrgh... Y-yesterday was an exception.
...I'm the one who told you about Ryudou Temple, so it would be a problem for me if something happened to you."

page18.text:
...
...I'm surprised.
Does Tohsaka feel responsible for what happened?

page19.text:
"Oh. Well, thanks for worrying about me, Tohsaka."
"I-it's not about you! I just wanted to know what happened to one of my intel sources!"

page20.text:
"Huh? I told you during yesterday's phone call. Caster and her Master are defeated. There's nothing at Ryudou Temple anymore."
Wait.
Why does she look so serious all of a sudden?

page21.text:
"What? Did I say something weird?"
"Yeah. It's not that I don't believe you, but I want to be sure. Did you really beat Caster?"

page22.text:
"...Hm. Even I can tell we won that fight.
Saber completely got rid of Caster. And Caster's Master..."
...was already dead by the time we arrived.

page23.text: "...Fine. Then, I want to talk about that. Come with me to the roof."
